## Historical audit — S0068

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/ablation_r1/ours_without_probes/C1/test/commons_199974832/trajectory.jsonl`. Only chunk 2 of 2 is visible.

| Evidence | Observation and interpretation |
|---|---|
| Line 10, student `model_request`, characters [0,303340) | The stated goal was an editable reconstruction from one indoor photograph. The student’s inferred scene was a woodworking workshop; the photograph itself is not visible to this audit. The program specifies many separate objects: room, window, shelves, planes, bench, vise, tools, kettle, bottle and nail bowl. These names and inventories are not independent confirmation of the reference. |
| Line 10, same event | A source-audit instruction reached the student before execution; it requested checks rather than identifying a measured defect. The subsequent complete program visibly adopted guards for dimensions, endpoints and unique keys, World initialization, descendant-mesh traversal and material copies. It also changed the booklet and foreground saws to transform their parts together. No separate teacher diagnosis is visible. |
| Line 10, same event | Multiple objects and composite parenting are evidenced in code, not independently verified as correctly connected or supported. The program assigns wood, metal and other colors, roughness, camera and lights; it does not evidence image textures. It specifies tool rotations and support heights, but actual pose, physical contact and reference fidelity remain unverified. |
| Line 10, same event | The runner reported step 1 `ok: true`, completed 16 render samples, saved a PNG and Blender scene, and supplied the render for comparison. This is execution/render success, not a visual or geometric correctness test. No camera, lighting or render defect is independently observable here because neither image is available to the auditor. |
| Lines 11–13, `codex_session`, `model_error`, `scene_error`, characters [0,4638), [0,1789), [0,3971) respectively | The post-render student session had the reference and render staged, but timed out after about 450 seconds with zero recorded tool calls. The scene loop propagated the timeout. No comparison, revised program, `DONE` or `SELECT` is visible. Staging images establishes availability, not successful inspection. |

**Outcome:** A successful first build and render were reported, followed by a **technical interruption** during review. Final submission and reconstruction correctness are unknown; this is neither evidence of an empty patch nor of an algorithmic failure. No autonomous diagnostic exploration is recorded, and the instructions prohibited diagnostic probes.

**Lessons and uncertainty:** Transferably, source guards and grouped transforms address identifiable implementation risks, while a completed render alone cannot certify geometry or appearance. The dense workshop inventory and chosen camera are task-specific hypotheses. Whether objects were cropped or occluded correctly, whether their parts actually meet, and whether framing, lighting and materials match the photograph remain unresolved. The unseen first chunk may contain additional evidence; none is assumed here.
